learning_lessons.title: python sequence iteration
learning_lessons.instruction: A loop visits a sequence in order. Initialize any accumulated state before the loop. On each iteration, read the current value and update that state once. Trace the state after every visit; check empty and one-element inputs separately.
examples:
total = 0
for value in [2, 3, -1]:
    total += value
# After each iteration: 2, 5, 4.
learning_lessons.language_notes: Python lists are indexed from zero. A for loop can visit values directly. Integers grow beyond fixed-width bounds, but time and memory limits still apply. Empty lists perform zero loop iterations.
learning_lessons.pattern_recognition: Use traversal when the requested result depends on inspecting each element. Decide what small state describes the already processed prefix; distinguish an aggregate from a position-dependent result.
learning_lessons.correctness: For the sum trace, total equals the sum of the already processed prefix. It is zero for an empty prefix; adding the next value preserves the invariant. When traversal ends, the prefix is the whole sequence.
learning_lessons.complexity: For n elements, traversal takes O(n) time and uses O(1) auxiliary state, excluding input storage. Search can stop earlier but still has O(n) worst-case time.

retrieval_check.prompt: Start total at zero, add 2, then 3. What is total?

exit_check.prompt: Start total at zero. Add 2, then 3, then -1. Write the final value as one digit.

learning_lessons.title: python linear search
learning_lessons.instruction: Inspect positions from left to right. Before visiting position i, earlier positions have already been checked. Compare the current value with the target. Stop at the first match when the task requests the first position; report absence only after every position has been checked.
examples:
values = [9, 5, 9]
for index, value in enumerate(values):
    # Visit index 0 first. It already matches target 9.
    pass
learning_lessons.language_notes: Python lists are indexed from zero. A for loop can visit values directly. Integers grow beyond fixed-width bounds, but time and memory limits still apply. Empty lists perform zero loop iterations.
learning_lessons.pattern_recognition: Use a linear scan when input has no useful order or index and any position might match. A first-occurrence requirement changes the stopping rule; duplicates and absence are separate test cases.
learning_lessons.correctness: Before visiting position i, no earlier position equals the target. A match at i is therefore the first match. If the scan ends without a match, every position has been checked and absence is justified.
learning_lessons.complexity: For n elements, traversal takes O(n) time and uses O(1) auxiliary state, excluding input storage. Search can stop earlier but still has O(n) worst-case time.

retrieval_check.prompt: In [9, 5, 9], which zero-based index is the first match for 9?

exit_check.prompt: Search [2, 4] for 3. Use -1 for absence. Write the returned integer.
